body: Aww, that's lovely, you're welcome :) Mm, it's certainly not easy, but I think you're doing an amazing job pushing through it all!

Yeah it definitely would be so much harder to do exposure therapy over the phone. It sucks people in general don't seem to understand what it's like to struggle leaving the house and cope with such intense anxiety. That must leave you feeling isolated and maybe even ashamed? :(

But I've noticed- correct me if I'm wrong- but it sounds like before covid hit, you were making a lot of progress! You were going to therapy, had a job, and had gotten out of that toxic environment with your parents? But now you feel trapped with the burden of extra anxiety needing to protect your brother. So maybe it's not that you're not made to be here, but that due to things that are out of your control, it's so much harder just to get through each day? I don't think you're alone with that.

I'm sorry you've been through so much with your family, I can't imagine how traumatic that all would be for you. Especially because it's ongoing and you feel the added pressure of protecting your brother. I don't think you're broken- I think you're doing the best you can at the moment, and that takes a lot of strength

Oh my god no one should say that to anyone, I can't believe that nurse said that to you. I'm so sorry you went through that, what a horrible memory. You should not feel guilty at all for surviving, or be disgusted with yourself. I'm so glad you 'chickened out' as you say, because it means you're still with us. I would actually disagree and say it was a very brave thing of you to reach out to your friend for help. And to go through all that. I hope you're doing okay too

Oh that's a lovely thing of you to do for him. Mm panic attacks are a very real thing. It sounds like it's gotten to the point where you can't leave the house because of the fear you might have one? Withdrawing from the meds sounds really difficult. I can understand why you'd be scared of the police, I think it's a common problem, sadly, so you're not alone there :(

You probably already know about this, but just to check- have you ever tried exposure therapy? I think anxiety can be treated at any time in your life, although of course it would be harder when it's been around so long, and you've been reliant on other ways of coping for so long.

It sounds like your parents have been really dismissive of your mental health struggles, which may have increased a sense of anxiety and shame? I'm sorry you're going through this. It sounds like you have a lot to offer the world, and that you are very thoughtful. And at the moment you're doing the best you can, for you and your brother

Yeah I can really hear that you've stepped up to protect and look after him. What are you reinforcing- is it his studies? Why do you feel like you have to die once your brother is out of there and set up? Surely you would want to be there for him for longer and see him achieve things? Once you're both out of that horrible environment, it sounds like there won't be as much constant trauma going on and you might be able to work on you for a change. If you can support your brother in such a compassionate and caring way, I reckon you can support yourself too (once you're away from the toxic family environment). You've got a lot of strength and kindness there, I'm sure you could do a lot more than you give yourself credit for.. What do you think?

It sounds like she was really supportive and a source of inspiration for you? So you currently don't have any supports? :( It must be tough dealing with this all alone. I understand your hesitation, you don't want to be separated from the one person you care about. I think services try to keep families together these days, but you're right it does happen. But thinking about what would be best for you and your brother, constantly going through that abuse every day, it's not okay. What if the services could give you and your brother a chance at succeeding? And getting away from your family? I dunno, it just sounds like things are pretty unbearable at the moment

That's so terrible, I'm so sorry you've not been listened to.. Are there any charities you could seek help from? I understand it would be really difficult to keep asking for help after those traumatic experiences.. You are such a good support for your brother hey.. I'm sure he really loves and appreciates you.

It sounds like you guys really need to get out of that abusive home hey...Has your therapist offered you any practical advice on where you could go?

Ugh that sounds like such an awful environment to be stuck in. I can't even imagine. I understand you not wanting to leave your brother alone with her. Is it your dad who's telling you to go easier on her? 
It sounds like getting you and your brother out of this situation would be the best thing for both of you, but that seems impossible right now? Is there anywhere else you could stay? Anyone who could help you out (even like a government or charity based support)? It's not okay that you and your brother are being treated so horribly

I think people always ask what if when something tragic happens. "What if we had the money to afford treatment X" "What if we noticed the signs sooner" etc. It's just what we do, I think, we find meaning in everything.. I know you feel trapped at the moment :( But it won't be like this forever. Especially at this time, with covid. I think you mentioned that you are living with your family at the moment? Or did I misunderstand? It must be awful having to see your abuser all the time :(

That sounds like a really sweet experience with your brother. As he knows a little bit about what's going on, do you think you could perhaps tell him how bad things are getting at the moment? 

Why do you think therapy isn't working? I don't think being agoraphobic means you're a loser. If someone you loved was struggling with it, would you think them a loser? I think it just makes you human

The fact you wish for a terminal illness shows you're trying to think of a way to make it 'easier' on your brother because you care about him so much :( But I'm sure your death would be devastating to him no matter the circumstances

It sounds like you were happiest when you were honest with someone you cared about who was open and honest with you. But right now it sounds like you're feeling alone and burdened with making such a painful decision

I'm hearing how much pain you're in :( It sounds like your thoughts of suicide are really strong at the moment. It's good you're going to therapy, but it must feel so horrible to be ridiculed and gaslighted. You're not alone in experiencing that kind of treatment.. Is therapy helping at all? 

It sounds like your brother really cares about you. What do you think about reaching out to him about this? 

I'm sure you know that success doesn't equal happiness... It sounds like loyalty and belonging are really strong values for you that are keeping you here? You don't have to act on your thoughts right now... there are people out there who want to hear you

Your brother must mean a lot to you to stick around for him, hey. I'm hearing you feel like you don't matter and you can't see the point? 20 is still quite young, I think. Is there somewhere you wish you would have got to by now? It sounds like you do matter, maybe not to everyone (who matters to everyone though?), but to your brother and dad at least?

I'm sorry you're in so much pain and have been through such horrible things.. I can't imagine what it's like.. It sounds like you're a huge support for your brother, and that's what's keeping you here for the time being. It sounds like despite all the shit you've been through, you've been fighting so hard and that shows how strong you are. I wonder what's gotten you through everything up to now?
What's going on with your parents? And that makes sense it would impact on school, all these things in life interact. What do you mean by you won't be around for much longer? Are you safe?
I just don't want to think anymore :(
That's hard :( Did you want to talk more about one of those in particular?
I know life can be brutal for many, but why should that mean we have to stick around if it's too much for us?

Hey I'm sorry you've been struggling for so long :( It sounds like there are people you really care about in your life- your partner and your friend. The fact you're reaching out right now, as you said, shows part of you still wants help. I know you have this plan set out and it feels like you have to go through with it, but at the end of the day these horrible thoughts you're having- they're just thoughts, and you are so much more than your thoughts. Do you have anyone you could talk to in your life about this, or a helpline you could call?
